qcm.title: Practice: Norwegian nouns, adjectives, tenses and modals

questions.prompt: What is the definite singular form of et møte?

options.explanation: -en is the masculine suffix; møte is neuter.
After a final -e, only -t is added.
A determiner alone does not make the noun definite.

questions.explanation: Neuter nouns take -et in the definite singular; a noun that already ends in -e just adds -t: et møte -> møtet.

links.label: Review: nouns: indefinite and definite forms

questions.prompt: Which definite singular forms of ei/en bok are accepted in Bokmål? Select all that apply.

options.explanation: -et is the neuter suffix.
That is the definite plural; bok has an irregular plural: bøker, bøkene.

questions.explanation: Bokmål allows feminine forms (ei bok, boka) and common-gender forms (en bok, boken). Be consistent within one text.

links.label: Review: nouns: indefinite and definite forms

options.explanation: The base form goes with masculine and feminine indefinite nouns.
-e is used in the plural and in definite phrases.

questions.explanation: Neuter singular indefinite adds -t to the adjective: et stort prosjekt.

options.explanation: Adjectives ending in -ig take no -t in the neuter.
That is the plural/definite form.

questions.explanation: Adjectives ending in -ig keep the base form in the neuter singular: et viktig møte, but viktige møter.

options.explanation: In a definite phrase the adjective takes -e.
The noun keeps its definite suffix as well (double definiteness).
rapport is masculine, so the determiner is den.

questions.explanation: A definite noun phrase with an adjective uses a determiner, the -e form of the adjective and the definite suffix on the noun.

questions.prompt: Complete: I går ___ jeg ferdig med rapporten. (bli)

options.explanation: I går places the event in a finished past time, which favours the preterite.
Present tense does not fit i går.
A participle needs har.

questions.explanation: Preterite for a completed event located in a finished past time; note V2 as well: I går ble jeg ...

links.label: Review: past tense: preterite versus perfect

questions.prompt: Complete: Jeg ___ i Oslo siden 2022, og jeg bor der fortsatt. (bo)

options.explanation: The preterite would present the situation as finished.
har is followed by the past participle bodd.
The participle needs the auxiliary har.

questions.explanation: Perfect tense for a situation that started in the past and continues now, typically with siden.

links.label: Review: past tense: preterite versus perfect

options.text: Jeg må sende rapporten i dag.
Jeg må å sende rapporten i dag.
options.explanation: No å after a modal verb.

options.text: Jeg må sender rapporten i dag.
options.explanation: The verb after a modal is an infinitive, not the present tense.

options.text: Jeg må sendt rapporten i dag.
options.explanation: A participle needs a perfect construction such as har sendt.

questions.explanation: Modal verbs (kan, må, skal, vil, bør) take a bare infinitive: må sende.

links.label: Review: modal verbs in work conversations
